subject: Mediflow VPC performance escalation — Q3 tuning request
messages:
From: Emma Ross <emma@mediflow.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@mediflow.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 95th p latency and intermittent 504s in our VPC

Hi Karthik / Redwood team,

We're seeing a persistent jump in p95 latency (from ~280ms to 1.8-2.2s) and an uptick in 504s across our private VPC since ~14:00 PDT yesterday. The spike correlates with a higher batch of inference traffic from our nightly enrichment job, but throttling the job only reduced errors slightly — latency remains elevated.

I've attached a trimmed p95 report and a heap snapshot from one of our app nodes. Our SLA window is at risk if this continues. Can you triage and advise immediate mitigations? We can approve brief configuration changes/reboots if needed.

Attachments: p95_latency_log_20280629.csv, heap_snapshot_20280629.txt

Thanks,
Emma Ross
CTO, Mediflow
emma@mediflow.com

On Fri, Jun 29, 2028 at 15:05 Redwood Support <support@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the alert — we received the logs and are looking into it.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emma Ross <emma@mediflow.com>, ops@mediflow.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 18:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 95th p latency and intermittent 504s in our VPC

Emma — thanks for the report and the attachments. We're treating this as a priority incident. Initial read: several of the inference hosts show elevated KV cache evictions and CPU steal during the 14:00-16:30 window; request fanout for the enrichment job likely exposed a pathologic batching pattern.

Immediate plan (short):
- Marcus will run a live triage to confirm KV eviction and identify whether we can restore warm-cache behavior with an async prefix cache restore.
- Temporary mitigation: reduce per-request batch size and enable conservative batching thresholds for the enrichment job (non-invasive config change).
- If latency doesn't improve within 60m we'll schedule a rolling restart of the model workers on the affected hosts (we'll coordinate times to avoid a full-window outage).

Can you confirm approval for rolling restarts and a non-invasive batch-size change? Also please share the window when you can accept brief degraded throughput (5-10 min windows).

I'm looping in Marcus and Lauren for visibility; Lauren, this is trending toward an SLA exposure for Mediflow (DL-8791) and may need an Exec sync if remediation doesn't stabilize in the next few hours.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 18:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 95th p latency and intermittent 504s in our VPC — triage notes

Quick triage notes:
- Confirmed: KV cache miss rate jumped ~7x on four worker instances (worker-3,4,7,8) between 14:05–15:40 PDT. Memory pressure on those hosts caused eviction of prefix caches.
- Observed higher kernel scheduling latency on hosts with mixed tenant I/O; likely noisy-neighbor storage IO during the enrichment job writeback.

Short-term remediation (we can execute in the next 30-45m):
1) Patch: apply runbook_vpc_kvcache_patch.diff — this reduces the KV cache eviction threshold and introduces a short-lived async prefetch for recently-seen prefixes. Non-disruptive patch; FDs won't change.
2) Config: reduce max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 1024 for the enrichment route only (config toggle).
3) If (1)-(2) don't bring p95 under 600ms within 45m, schedule rolling restarts for the four affected workers (staggered 5-min overlap).

Risk: rolling restarts will cause brief drop in concurrency per shard; we'll keep concurrency throttle and routing fallbacks active.

I'll prepare the patch and a checklist. Need Mediflow ops confirmation for the config toggle and permission to do 4-staged restarts.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emma Ross <emma@mediflow.com>, ops@mediflow.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 19:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Mediflow VPC performance escalation — proposed immediate actions

Emma / Carlos — proposed immediate actions we can execute now (non-disruptive first):
- Toggle route config: reduce enrichment max_batch_tokens from 2048 to 1024 (apply to route T-enrich-01). Expected p95 improvement: 30-45%.
- Apply runbook_vpc_kvcache_patch.diff (hot patch) to affected worker pool; this adjusts eviction thresholds and enables a short async prefix prefetch (no restart).
- Monitor p95 for 30m post-change. If still >700ms, proceed with staged rolling restarts for workers 3/4/7/8 (5-min stagger).

Mutual action plan (MAP):
- Mediflow ops to confirm approval for config change and patch (reply all).
- Redwood to apply changes and monitor (we'll provide a dedicated dashboard link).
- If stabilization fails by 20:00 PDT, Exec sync requested (Lauren will join).

Please confirm 'approve' for the two non-disruptive steps.

Thanks,
Karthik
